source_text:
palam cunctis sicut ipse praedixit apparuit et sedentibus in tenebris manifestum uitae lumen effulsit, et iniustitia perfidorum pectus obsessum postposita propria ac reiecta salute tenebras potius caecitate cordis elegit.\'
Frequentat ubique atque manifestat prophetatio cunctorum, qui sancto spiritu praemonente aduentus Domini metatores esse sortiti sunt. hunc lumen saeculo datum et diem nobis salutis exortum uiuificandis quoque in eum credentibus destinatum docet hoc in psalmis spiritus sanctus et ostendit dicens: lapis quem reprobauerunt aedificantes hic factus est in caput anguli: a Domino factus est iste, et adest mirabilis in oculis nostris. iste dies est quem fecit Dominus, ambulemus et iocundemur in eo. in hoc die nos ambulare Paulus quoque apostolus praecipiens et docens ac praemonens dicit: nunc enim propius est nobis salus quam cum credidimus. nox praecessit, dies autem adpropinquauit. abiciamus opera tenebrarum et induamur arma lucis, sicut in die honeste ambulemus. id est in Christo et mandatis eius, cuius lumine ac monitis luminati et in claritate diei eius inuenti proximam nobis salutem credulitatis in eum mente conspicimus.
thought_title: Christ the day of salvation, and walking in his light
orientation: The author is arguing that the prophets universally foretold Christ's coming as light and day of salvation, and that Paul commands believers to walk in that day.
pass_a_gloss: He appeared openly to all, just as he himself foretold, and the manifest light of life shone forth upon those sitting in darkness, and the besieged breast of the faithless, having set aside its own and rejected salvation, chose rather darkness through blindness of heart. The prophecy of all those who were allotted to be the markers-out of the Lord's coming, with the Holy Spirit forewarning, makes this frequent everywhere and makes it manifest. The Holy Spirit teaches and shows this in the psalms, saying: the stone which the builders rejected, this one has become the head of the corner; this is done by the Lord, and it is wonderful in our eyes. This is the day which the Lord has made; let us walk and rejoice in it. Paul also the apostle, commanding and teaching and forewarning, says that we should walk in this day: for now salvation is nearer to us than when we believed. The night has passed, but the day has drawn near. Let us cast off the works of darkness and put on the armor of light, let us walk honestly as in the day. That is, in Christ and in his commandments, by whose light and warnings we have been enlightened, and being found in the brightness of his day, we perceive with the mind the salvation of faith in him that is near to us.

choices.why: Keeps the literal surveying metaphor of the prophets as those who mark out the Lord's coming in advance.
Literal rendering preserving the ablative of means and the biblical idiom.
Literal rendering of the psalm quotation, matching the source's architectural metaphor.
Literal rendering of Paul's military metaphor, preserving 'arma' as armor.
Literal rendering of the Pauline ethical command, keeping the adverb's moral sense.

choices.why: Preserves the gerundive force of 'uiuificandis' and the dative of advantage.

pass_b_english: He appeared openly to all, just as he himself foretold, and the clear light of life shone forth upon those sitting in darkness; but the besieged heart of the faithless, casting aside and rejecting its own salvation, chose darkness instead through blindness of heart.

The prophecy of all those who were allotted by the Holy Spirit's forewarning to be the markers-out of the Lord's coming makes this known everywhere and openly. The Holy Spirit teaches and shows in the Psalms that this light was given to the world, and that this day of salvation dawned for us, destined also for those who are to be made alive by believing in him, saying: "The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner; this is the Lord's doing, and it is marvelous in our eyes. This is the day which the Lord has made; let us walk and rejoice in it" (Psalms 118:22-24).

The apostle Paul also commands, teaches, and forewarns us to walk in this day, saying: "For now our salvation is nearer than when we believed. The night has passed, and the day has drawn near. Let us cast off the works of darkness and put on the armor of light; let us walk honestly as in the day" (Romans 13:11-13). That is, in Christ and his commandments, enlightened by his light and his warnings, and found in the brightness of his day, we perceive with our minds the salvation that is near to us through faith in him.

last_rejected.why: Latin 'metatores' means harvesters/gatherers, not 'markers-out'. The English renders the term nonsense, altering agency.
last_rejected.ruling: 'metatores' means surveyors/markers-out of a camp; 'harvesters' is wrong. English 'markers-out' is correct.
